ST-07.title: Trade Plan "Abandon" modal has no focus trap or restoration
ST-07.notes: Hand-rolled Abandon modal overlay in src/pages/TradePlan.js replaced with the existing Radix-based Dialog/DialogContent primitive (src/components/ui/dialog.js), same as TradeReflectionModal.js and other modals in the app. Root-caused and fixed a real focus-restoration bug during implementation (not just following the decision record blindly): Radix's default onCloseAutoFocus focuses context.triggerRef, which is only populated by <DialogTrigger> - this integration uses a plain trigger Button (controlled open/onOpenChange), so triggerRef was always null and the default handler's preventDefault() call was suppressing FocusScope's own fallback restore, leaving focus at document.body on every close path. Fixed via ref={abandonTriggerRef} on the trigger Button + explicit onCloseAutoFocus override. Caught via REAL browser testing (system chromium, temporary local-only playwright.config.js override, reverted before commit - not shipped), not just code reading - the first attempt failed this exact assertion, confirming the bug was real. 4 new Playwright tests added (SC-E03-17 to SC-E03-20 in tests/e2e/epic03-v34-frontend.spec.js): focus-on-open, Tab-trap-cycle, Escape-closes-with-focus-restore, Cancel-closes-with-focus-restore. All 20 tests in that file plus all 33 in tests/e2e/trade-plan.spec.js verified passing against a real browser - no regressions. Corrected docs/design/.../abandon-modal-focus-trap/decision_record.md's §3 table: the drafted tab order (textarea->Abandon Plan->Cancel) didn't match the modal's actual, deliberately-unchanged button DOM order (Cancel-then-Submit) - reordering the DOM to match the draft would have flipped the visual button layout, contradicting the same record's own 'visual design unaffected' constraint, so the record was corrected to match tested reality instead (per LL-v3.4-P3-03 intent-check: full non-escaping Tab cycle is the governing intent, satisfied either way). Head of UX & Design sign-off (agent-mediated): approved on first review; noted two non-blocking follow-ups (decision record wording fix - applied in this same commit; additional Playwright coverage for backdrop-click/successful-submit focus-restore paths - not added, since they share the same non-branching onCloseAutoFocus code path already verified via Escape/Cancel, reviewer judged this an acceptable non-blocking gap).

ST-09.title: .gitleaks.toml's global [[allowlists]] blocks use an invalid schema
ST-09.notes: Downloaded gitleaks v8.21.2 binary directly (not installed in this environment) to verify locally, matching the version the file's own pre-existing comment says was used previously. Baseline scan with the OLD config found 3 unsuppressed generic-api-key findings (STORAGE_KEY pattern) in claude/cycles/2026-06-26__release-v6.3/qa_evidence_EPIC-03.md, docs/frontend/prompts/ai-briefing-progressive-disclosure-v1.md, and src/components/dashboard/home/AiDailyBriefing.js - confirming the bare [[allowlists]] schema bug was real and actively causing false-positive CI noise, not just theoretical. Rewrote all 4 blocks: 2 pre-existing correctly-formed [[rules]] blocks (github-pat, generic-api-key for test_secrets_scanning_hook.py) left unchanged; 'localStorage key strings' became a 2nd [[rules.allowlists]] entry under the existing generic-api-key rule (paths extended to include src/*.js, which the original .md-only paths missed - one of the 3 real findings was in the .js source itself; added a 2nd regex for markdown-prose-quoted form); 'Test fixture synthetic credentials' + 'Alpaca test stubs' merged into ONE global [allowlist] singular table (verified via isolated empirical test that this form actually suppresses, since neither pattern ties to one specific currently-firing rule ID - confirmed via a clean gitleaks detect with no config at all showing zero findings for those two files' patterns). Post-fix gitleaks detect --no-git: 0 leaks (all 3 real findings suppressed). Full CI-equivalent scan (gitleaks detect --verbose, matching secret-scanning.yml's exact command) found 2 more findings but on a commit confirmed (git merge-base --is-ancestor) to be reachable ONLY via gh-pages, not main - out of CI's actual scan scope (push/PR triggers only main/develop; GitHub Actions checkout doesn't fetch unrelated branches). Scoped re-scan (--log-opts=main): 0 leaks, matching CI's real surface. tests/test_secrets_scanning_hook.py (previously skip-guarded, gitleaks not normally on PATH) run with gitleaks available: 3/3 pass. Full backend suite: 925 passed, 2 skipped, no regressions. Cybersecurity & Trust Lead sign-off (agent-mediated): approved, independently re-ran every verification step (before/after scans, main-scoped scan, regression test, regex narrowness review, merge-rationale check against gitleaks' own README schema docs) rather than trusting the report.
